gap: No result ChatGPT got states that its #1 pick, the UGREEN CM642 fan enclosure, is the most expensive of the 40Gbps NVMe enclosures priced here at $109.99 on us.ugreen.com, against $89.99 for the TerraMaster D1 SSD Plus and the fan-cooled Sabrent EC-U4TN, $99.99 for the OWC Express 1M2 (ChatGPT showed $129.99) and $84.90 for ACASIS's fan model. It also doesn't state that one named owner saw CM642 writes fall from about 700 to 300 MB/s after a minute or two and blamed the ASM2464PD bridge chip overheating.
standout_why: Compared with the results ChatGPT cited and the top results. itechguides (cited) lists Amazon prices for the fanless UGREEN ($105.99), OWC Express 1M2 ($99.99) and ACASIS TBU405 Pro ($72.19), but not the CM642 fan model, TerraMaster or Sabrent, and has no sustained-write data for any 40Gbps DIY enclosure. soldermag (rank 5) gives no prices and says it never measured sustained performance. OWC's own pages (cited) show no price on owc.com. Tom's Hardware (cited) has a 2022 date and covers the PA40SU but not the CM642. Our current page lists the PCWorld 450 GB pass for the CM642 but has no same-day maker-store prices and no long-copy failure report for the CM642. The price comparison adds to what itechguides partly covers. The CM642 owner measurement is new.
decides: This weakens ChatGPT's #1 pick without overturning it. The CM642 costs $20 more than the fanless TerraMaster D1 SSD Plus ($89.99), which PCWorld found faster than UGREEN's CM850 on long copies. It also costs $20 more than Sabrent's fan model with the same ASM2464PD chip ($89.99). The only owner report on the CM642 describes bridge-chip slowdown and dropouts, against PCWorld's clean 450 GB write. Unless a test shows the CM642's fan holding speed past PCWorld's 450 GB, the D1 SSD Plus at $89.99 is the value pick for long copies. The CM642 stays in as the fan choice, but its premium has to be earned by a test.

findings.label: Owner long-write result (where it loses)
findings.value: About 700 MB/s falling to 300 MB/s after 'a minute or two' of real NTFS writes with a WD Red SN700 4TB. The same drive held 1100–1200 MB/s inside a desktop. A Kingston KC3000 2TB and an Apacer AS2280Q4U disconnected after a few minutes of writing.
findings.source_title: Random access rants - my new USB4 enclosure (noise.paulos.cz, 2025-08-03)
findings.note: One owner, informal test, no logged temperatures and no GB written before the drop. The author concluded the ASM2464PD bridge was 'likely overheating' and switched to a Satechi USB4 NVMe SSD Pro with a Lexar NM790. This conflicts with PCWorld's 450 GB pass, so it marks the CM642 as unproven rather than failed.
